label: thm:geometric
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:geometric}
Suppose a width-one body $K$ has circumradius $R\ge0.609$, and let $T$ be a balanced contact tetrahedron. If the six squared-edge deficits of $T$ are nonnegative and have sum $D\le0.06$, then
\[
 \operatorname{Vol}(K)\ge B(D).
\]
head: environment
name: Near-Jung geometric estimate

label: lem:sharpD
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Sharp deficit comparison

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $P=I-\frac14\mathbf1\mathbf1^t$, and let $\Delta$ have off-diagonal entries $\delta_{ij}$ and zero diagonal. On $H=\mathbf1^\perp$, the centered Gram matrix is
\[
 G=\frac12(P+P\Delta P).
\]
Since $\|\Delta\|_{\rm op}\le D<1$, $G$ is positive definite on $H$. Put $r_i=\sum_j\delta_{ij}$ and $z=(r-(D/2)\mathbf1)/8$. The equal-radius identities give
\[
 b\cdot(x_i-b)=z_i,\qquad |b|^2=z^t(G|_H)^{-1}z.
\]
For completeness, the diagonal entries of $G$ are $3/8-r_i/4+D/16$, whereas their average is $3/8-D/16$; subtracting the equal-radius identities proves the first formula.

For fixed $D$, the function in the last display is convex in the six deficits, because
\[
 z^tG^{-1}z=\sup_{v\in H}\{2z\cdot v-v^tGv\}
\]
is a supremum of affine functions. The deficit simplex has vertices with one deficit equal to $D$ and all others zero. At such a vertex, $|z|^2=D^2/64$ and $Gz=((2+D)/4)z$. Hence every vertex value is $D^2/[16(2+D)]$. Convexity proves the bound. Substitution in \eqref{eq:Didentity} gives $2D/(2+D)\le16d$, equivalent to \eqref{eq:sharpD}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
A Gram matrix of three incident edge vectors has diagonal entries $a,b,c$ and off-diagonal entries $(a+b-d)/2$, $(a+c-e)/2$, $(b+c-f)/2$, where $a,\ldots,f$ are the six squared lengths. This matrix is affine in the deficits. At a vertex of their simplex, direct calculation gives determinant
\[
 \frac12-\frac D4-\frac{D^2}{4}=\frac{(1-D)(2+D)}4.
\]
The six vertex matrices are positive definite for the present range of $D$. Concavity of $\log\det$ therefore bounds the determinant of every convex combination below by this common value. This concavity follows, for example, by differentiating twice along a line of positive matrices: the second derivative is $-\operatorname{tr}(G^{-1}G'G^{-1}G')\le0$. Finally $\operatorname{Vol}(T)=\sqrt{\det G}/6$.

label: lem:faceinclusion
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Circumradius-aware face region

title: Proof
body_md:
Express $p=\sum_i\mu_i x_i$ using the face vertices. For $y\in K$, the inequalities $|y-x_i|\le1$ imply
\[
 |y|^2-2p\cdot y+R^2\le1.
\]
For $x=p+tn$, use $n\cdot y\ge-R$ to get
\[
 |x-y|^2\le1-R^2+|p|^2+t^2+2t(R+h)\le1
\]
whenever $t$ is in \eqref{eq:newface}. Equation \eqref{eq:balls} proves the inclusion.

label: lem:Cmonotone
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Cmonotone}
The function $C(R)$ is strictly decreasing on $[R_1,R_0]$.
head: environment

label: eq:crude-ranges
title: Proof
body_md:
All estimates in this proof are deliberately rounded outward. On the slightly larger interval $0.604\le R\le0.611$ we have
\begin{equation}\label{eq:crude-ranges}
 0.4898\le s<0.497,\qquad
 0.8736<q<0.88,\qquad
 1.36<H<1.38,
 \qquad -H'<2.28.
\end{equation}
Indeed $q=1-2cR+c^2$ and
$H'=-4R-2c+4cq$.

Write $n=q^2-8s^5$. Then $n<0.55$ and
$n'=-4cq-40s^4<-2.70$. Hence the derivative of the first term in \eqref{eq:Cdef} satisfies
\[
 \left(\frac{n}{3H}\right)'
 =\frac{n'H-nH'}{3H^2}
 <\frac{-2.70(1.36)+0.55(2.28)}{3(1.38)^2}
 <-0.42.
\]

For the second term put
\[
 A_R=\frac4{3RH},\qquad
 L=2R-c-1,
 \qquad
 K(R,w)=\frac{P(s-w)}{(s-w)^2}.
\]
Then it equals $A_RJ_R$, where
\[
 J_R=\int_0^Lw^2K(R,w)\,\,\mathrm d w.
\]
On our interval $L<0.108$, $1-R>0.389$, $m<0.636$, and the six positive terms in $K$ give $K<6$. At fixed $w$, differentiating those six terms shows $K_R\le7K$: the logarithmic derivative of each term is at most $3/s$, except for $s^2(s-w)$, whose logarithmic derivative is at most $2/s+1/(1-R)<7$. Also $A_R<1.64$ and
\[
 \frac{A_R'}{A_R}=-\frac1R-\frac{H'}H<0.05.
\]
Consequently
\[
 J_R\le2L^3,
 \qquad
 J_R'\le12L^2+14L^3<0.158,
 \qquad
 A_RJ_R<0.0042.
\]
It follows that
\[
 (A_RJ_R)'<1.64(0.158)+0.05(0.0042)<0.260.
\]
Combining the two estimates gives $C'(R)<-0.16<0$.

label: lem:Phi-monotone
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Phi-monotone}
For every fixed $z\in[0,c]$, the function $R\mapsto\Phi_R(z)$ is nonincreasing on $[R_1,R_0]$.
head: environment

label: eq:Xlog
title: Proof
body_md:
For $0<z<c$ put
\[
 K=\frac{P(R-z)}{(R-z)^2},
 \qquad X=\frac{x}{\gamma^2}.
\]
The six positive monomials in $K$ give $K_R/K<7$ by the same termwise differentiation as in \cref{lem:Cmonotone}. Moreover $-H'/H<1.68$. From \eqref{eq:xformula} and $\gamma^2=1-1/(4R^2)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Xlog}
 \frac{X_R}{X}
 =-\frac{z}{1-Rz}-\frac1R-\frac1{R-z}
   -\frac{2}{R(4R^2-1)}<-9.9.
\end{equation}
Thus the product $KX/H$ strictly decreases.

It remains only to check the two correction factors. The quantity
$\alpha=1/(2R)-R$ decreases, so $1+\alpha X/2$ decreases. Also
\[
 y=\alpha X+\frac12R^2X^2.
\]
The first term decreases, while
\[
 \frac\,\mathrm d{\,\mathrm d R}\log(R^2X^2)
 =\frac2R+2\frac{X_R}{X}<3.32-19.8<0.
\]
Hence $y$, and therefore $1+y+y^2$, decreases. This proves the claim; the endpoints $z=0,c$ follow by continuity.

title: Proof
body_md:
The square-root bounds follow by squaring. For $\pi$, use Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan\frac15-4\arctan\frac1{239}
\]
and the alternating series for $\arctan$. For the lower bound use the lower partial sum through degree $15$ for $\arctan(1/5)$ and the upper partial sum through degree $5$ for $\arctan(1/239)$; for the upper bound use the upper partial sum through degree $13$ for $\arctan(1/5)$ and the lower partial sum through degree $3$ for $\arctan(1/239)$. Direct cross multiplication places the resulting two rational numbers strictly between the displayed bounds. For $\arcsin(1/3)$ use
\[
 \arcsin x=\sum_{n\ge0}
 \frac{\binom{2n}{n}}{4^n(2n+1)}x^{2n+1}.
\]
At $x=1/3$ the ratio of consecutive positive terms is less than $1/9$; the partial sum through $n=7$, together with $9/8$ times the next term as an upper bound for the tail, lies between the two displayed rationals.

title: Proof
body_md: If $R\le R_1$, use \eqref{eq:small-analytic}. If $R_1\le R\le R_0$, use \eqref{eq:intermediate-final}. If $R\ge R_0$, \cref{thm:geometric}, \cref{lem:sharpD}, and \eqref{eq:near-jung-final} apply. These three ranges cover the full Jung interval. Scaling from width one to width $w$ proves \eqref{eq:main}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The proof has no finite mesh or computer-assisted step, but it is not optimized. The near-Jung estimate loses information in the face symmetrization, in the derivative bounds for dihedral angles, and in the lower estimate for the additional face-edge sectors. The intermediate radial estimate deliberately replaces the exact angular Jacobian by the second-order bound \eqref{eq:B-upper} and then keeps only four Taylor coefficients at the endpoint. Thus $0.41275$ should not be interpreted as a limit of the contact-tetrahedron or radial methods.
